pageCache.pageTitle: Charterhouse Square School - Private School & Nursery, London
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Charterhouse Square School
We have high aspirations for the children at Charterhouse Square School, where our pupils flourish both in and out of the classroom. Located in the heart of the City of London, within the leafy square of Barbican, we do things a little differently. As a co-educational City prep school, our pupils aged 3 to 11 achieve exceptional academic results within a nurturing, home-from-home environment. Celebrating individuality while fostering a strong sense of togetherness, we instil a confidence that prepares our children for life beyond our doors, paving the way for success at leading senior schools. We'd love you to come and visit our school and see for yourself what makes Charterhouse Square a special private school in London.
The confidence for... Creative and Self-Expression.
Whether through oracy, sports, arts, or creative pursuits, our students are given the freedom to express themselves, building teamwork, resilience and a love for discovery that shapes their personal growth.
The confidence to... Achieve Academic Excellence.
Our pupils are encouraged to embrace challenges and strive beyond expectations. With a curriculum designed to inspire, they consistently achieve results well above the national average.
The confidence for... Future Success.
We prepare our pupils for their next steps with the skills and self-assurance they need to thrive. Year after year, our students secure places at some of London’s most prestigious schools, ready to take on new challenges.
Meet our Headteacher, Tushi Gorasia
Tushi joins Charterhouse Square School with over a decade of senior leadership experience across state, international, and independent schools. She is dedicated to creating a supportive, inclusive, and innovative learning environment for every child. "We pride ourselves on high academic standards, exceptional pastoral care and a very loving and nurturing environment." -Tushi Gorasia, Headteacher
Recognised for innovation and creativity
We’re proud to be recognised nationally for the creative, ambitious and forward-thinking learning experiences we give our pupils.
Commended — Independent School of the Year for Best Use of Education Technology
Highly Commended — Excellence in Visual Arts & Creative Writing
Shortlisted — Independent Prep School of the Year
A place where your child's passion for learning comes to life!
Watch our video to discover more about the vibrant and nurturing life at Charterhouse Square School.
Meet us in person
Come and see our fantastic school in action during an Open Event or Nursery Viewing Day. We can promise you a warm welcome to Charterhouse Square School.
FACILITIES & LOCATION
A welcoming and nurturing environment.
Charterhouse Square School has a character and ethos all of its own. We cultivate a family atmosphere with no school uniforms and build strong relationships on a first-name basis between teachers and pupils - all in our unique central location in the City of London. Our impressive terrace of seven interlinked buildings offers remarkably spacious and vibrant, light-filled rooms, stretching along one side of Charterhouse Square with views across the serene garden and the historic Charterhouse. Within these interconnected townhouses, thoughtfully designed spaces, including those for art, music and indoor play, sit alongside a dining area where children enjoy fresh, nutritious meals each day, creating an environment that supports both focus and creativity. Being based in the City opens the door to extraordinary experiences beyond the classroom. From rooftop lessons and performances to sport at Coram’s Fields and adventures at Three Corners Playground, our pupils make full use of the outstanding opportunities on our doorstep. They regularly visit London’s museums, galleries and theatres, learning to engage with the world around them in a way that feels natural and inspiring.
Accredited Allergy School
We are proud to announce that Charterhouse Square School has been officially recognised as an Allergy School by the Natasha Allergy Research Foundation. This important accreditation highlights our commitment to providing a safe, inclusive environment for every member of our community. Guided by the Foundation’s values - Empower, Include, Protect - we continue to raise awareness, uphold best practices, and ensure that every pupil and staff member can enjoy meals at school with confidence and support.
See where a Charterhouse Square education can take your child.
Every year, our pupils secure places at some of London’s most respected senior schools – from City of London and Highgate to Alleyn’s, JAGS and UCS. But it’s not just about academic success; it’s about confidence, readiness, and the right next step for every child. Discover our recent 11+ outcomes, scholarship awards, and the schools our children move on to in our latest destinations brochure.
Good Schools Guide Review
The GSG says: "Bright, neat, colourful classrooms were full of interested, happy and very polite children and the atmosphere of the school is extremely warm and friendly. Pupils who were leaving told us how they’ll miss Charterhouse ‘sooo much’, especially the teachers. ‘What I really like about the teachers is that they are all so friendly."
Muddy Stilettos Review: 2024
Muddy's says: "A dynamic co-ed school for 3-11 year olds with strong academics and excellent pastoral care, set in a quiet leafy square in Barbican."
Charterhouse Chats
Charterhouse Chats is a pupil-led podcast, created and hosted by our Year 5 and Year 6 pupils. With new episodes released each month, it offers an authentic insight into school life, shaped by the voices of those who live it every day. Listen to our first episode: What makes learning fun at school?
Follow us on Social Media to stay connected with the latest news and life at Charterhouse Square School

This recognition celebrates our Architecture and Urban Design Initiative, which gave pupils the opportunity to explore their creativity through art, digital design and model-making. Inspired by the world of architecture, pupils developed their own concepts and brought their ideas to life, before showcasing their work as part of Clerkenwell Design Week. A fantastic recognition of the imagination, creativity and ambition of our pupils, and the opportunities we create for learning beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our School Vision and Values - Independent School in London
pageCache.text:
School Ethos and Aims
Our school is a little different
At Charterhouse Square School, we believe that for children to truly excel, they need to feel happy, safe, and supported. This guiding principle is at the heart of everything we do. Academic excellence is woven into our everyday experience, but our approach is about much more than just academic success – it’s about nurturing confident, curious individuals who are ready for life beyond the classroom. From the very start in Nursery, children are welcomed into a close-knit, family-like environment, creating a sense of stability and strong friendships. We pride ourselves on our inclusive atmosphere, where children don’t wear a school uniform and use first names between staff and pupils. It’s a small thing, but it speaks to the mutual respect and individuality we encourage every day. We encourage every child to step outside their comfort zone, to grow not just academically but personally, with a strong focus on building a lifelong love of learning in a place where children feel empowered, confident, and ready to embrace challenges.
1. Provide an education that is academically rigorous, thoughtfully designed and dynamically delivered.
2. Create an environment that is forward-thinking, happy and inclusive, recognising every member of the Charterhouse Square community as having a special part to play in who we are.
3. Stay up-to-date with the changing nature of selective senior schools, developing prepared, confident and resilient young people who are prepared to take risks and challenge themselves.
Welcome to Charterhouse Square School
Our pupils are empowered to embrace challenges and step out of their comfort zones, encouraging them to push themselves to achieve at the very highest levels while developing as confident, articulate and self-motivated individuals.

Admissions Process for Nursery
Joining us is straightforward.
Apply for a place at our exceptional school and put your child on the path to a fantastic educational experience. We have designed our admissions process to be as easy as possible and we will happily guide you every step of the way. The main point of entry to Charterhouse Square School is at three years old. Children must turn three before 1st September of their admission year. Children may be registered from birth to 30th April of the year preceding their admission year. Please see our steps to enrolment outlined below. Occasional Nursery places may become available throughout the year, so we warmly encourage families to contact our Admissions Team to discuss availability.
If you have any questions about joining us at Charterhouse Square School, please click the link below to get in touch.
Experience the welcoming atmosphere of Charterhouse Square first-hand by paying us a visit once your child reaches their first birthday. We look forward to meeting you to show you around and give you an insight into school life. Please book a Nursery Viewing Day using the link below.
When you are ready to take the next step, simply complete the online application form and pay a registration fee of £180 (non-refundable). This will enable us to start our admissions process and include your application in the ballot.
We offer 52 places in Nursery each year. Where applications exceed the number of places available, a fair and transparent ballot is held. All completed applications received by the deadline are entered into a random draw, which for September 2027 entry will take place on 6 May 2026. Families are notified by telephone and email shortly afterwards. Registered siblings automatically receive a place, provided their brother or sister is attending Charterhouse Square School in their first term of entry. The ballot applies to Nursery entry only. For all other year group entries, please follow the link below:
Successful applicants are contacted after the ballot has taken place. They are then sent an offer pack and invited to attend an Open Morning. Unsuccessful applicants will be contacted asking if they wish for their child to remain on the waiting list. Please ensure you keep us informed of any changes to your contact information.
Once the school has received the acceptance form and deposit, our Admissions Manager will be in touch to confirm receipt.

Please note the below in reference to our admissions process. Our friendly admissions team will be on hand at any time during the process to help answer questions you may have.
You will receive confirmation by email once both the completed application form and the registration fee are received. Please get in touch if you do not hear from us, as without the completed application and registration fee, we will be unable to include your child in the ballot.
Acceptance Deposit is made to secure your child’s place. This is held by us until your child leaves the school, at which point the deposit is refunded, provided your account has been settled in full.

pageCache.text:
Early Years
Early Years: for children aged 3 - 5
Our staff in Early Years are committed to giving every child a wonderful start to school life. As part of our early years education, every activity is planned so that the girls and boys can try things out for themselves, exploring and developing their capabilities along the way. We know that happy children make good learners so our early learning Nursery Room is designed to make learning as fun as possible for our youngest children.
Our topic-based approach allows us to cover a broad range of subjects.
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, allowing children to explore the world around them. This framework is integrated into all areas of learning through a themed topic each half term. Whether it’s transport, animals, celebrations, or space, we bring these to life through activities linked to areas such as expressive arts and design, personal, social and emotional development and understanding the world.
Reading and Writing
Before and after school care
Your Child's Journey
Building a love of language and reading.
Cultivating a love of reading is a key feature of our literacy teaching in the Early Years, alongside developing fine motor skills for writing. Each child’s progress is closely monitored, enabling us to tailor our provision to their needs. As they learn individual phonics sounds, they will learn to blend and segment these to build their reading skills, and we introduce reading books when they are ready to benefit from them. We ensure that every child takes home a book each night to keep them stimulated and engaged, while continuously practising and expanding their vocabulary. As a school, we adopt a text-based approach to literacy lessons, thoroughly exploring books linked to topics so that children can immerse themselves in the text. We use these texts to create focused activities that develop reading, comprehension, and writing skills. Each session also incorporates free-choice play, allowing children to explore their interests and skills in an engaging environment. Alongside reading, we develop fine motor skills for writing through both play and more structured teaching. We guide the children on the technical aspects of letter formation and spelling, while also encouraging them to express themselves with confidence - the most important attribute we aim for them to develop during the Early Years.
Meet us in person
Come and see our fantastic school in action during an Open Event or Nursery Viewing Day. We can promise you a warm welcome to Charterhouse Square School.
Building strong foundations in Maths.
We lay strong foundations in both literacy and mathematics on which pupils can build their future academic success. Through direct teaching and play, we introduce key mathematical concepts such as numbers, measurement, patterns, and shapes. The children learn that maths is about engaging with the world around them and discover that it can be challenging, stimulating, and creative. Throughout the school, we use White Rose Maths to help children develop their conceptual understanding by using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and abstract thinking. This inclusive approach provides numerous opportunities to explore and apply concepts through play, helping children to grasp the ‘why’ behind maths.

pageCache.pageTitle: Private School Inspection Reports - Charterhouse Square School
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
ISI Inspection Report 2026: Standards Met Across All Areas
We are proud to share the outcomes of our latest ISI inspection, which recognised the strength of Charterhouse Square School’s education, culture and community. The inspection highlighted our welcoming and purposeful environment, where pupils are known as individuals and supported to develop confidence, independence and resilience. Inspectors also recognised the breadth of our curriculum, the strong relationships between pupils and staff, and the many opportunities pupils have to take responsibility, think creatively and contribute positively to school life. This inspection was conducted under the ISI framework introduced in 2023, which assesses schools across five key areas: - Leadership, management and governance - Quality of education, training and recreation - Pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing - Pupils’ social and economic education and contribution to society - Safeguarding Charterhouse Square School met all standards across each area of the inspection.
ISI 'Excellent in all areas' INSPECTION REPORT 2023
We are delighted to announce that Charterhouse Square has been judged by the ISI to be ‘excellent in all areas’. In April 2023, ISI inspectors examined both our compliance and educational standards. In an exceptionally thorough process, Parents, staff, and Upper House children were invited to complete questionnaires, over 70 lessons were observed, and the majority of staff were interviewed in some capacity. In addition, children’s books, teacher’s planning and all school procedures and policies were scrutinised. Charterhouse Square School has achieved the highest category of ‘excellent’ in both areas ‘quality of pupils’ academic and other achievements’ and ‘quality of pupils’ personal development’. In addition, all eight areas of the compliance inspection were met. This judgement is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our teaching teams and recognises what a very special place Charterhouse Square is.
ISI 'Excellent in all areas' INSPECTION REPORT 2019
"The school meets the standards in the schedule to the Education (Independent School Standards) Regulations 2014, and relevant requirements of the statutory framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage, and associated requirements. The curriculum is documented, supported by appropriate plans and schemes of work for the pupils and covers the required breadth of material. The teaching enables pupils to make good progress, encompasses effective behaviour management and is supported by suitable resources. A suitable framework for the assessment of pupils’ performance is in place. Arrangements are made to safeguard and promote the welfare of pupils by means that pay due regard to current statutory guidance. Pupils are properly supervised; admission and attendance registers are maintained, as required, and there is a strategic approach to risk assessment."
SIS INSPECTION REPORT 2016
In 2016, Charterhouse Square School was inspected by the School Inspection Service (SIS). The school met all requirements of the Education (Independent School Standards) Regulations 2014, the Equality Act 2010 and the Early Years Foundation Stage, with Outstanding judgements in all inspection categories.

pageCache.pageTitle: Private School Upper House, In London - Charterhouse Square
pageCache.text:
Upper House
Upper House: for children aged 8 - 11
As our children enter their final years at Charterhouse Square School, we continue to empower them to make excellent academic progress as they prepare for life in secondary school. During the key years for exam preparation, the children continue to focus highly on the core subjects of Literacy and Maths, while still maintain a diverse curriculum, which includes the creative subjects and PE. In the first term of the Star Room (Year 6), our oldest pupils spend time honing their exam technique by practising past papers, practising their interview skills and shifting to more independent learning.
A curriculum blending breadth and depth.
We take immense pride in offering a well-rounded curriculum that blends both breadth and depth. Our approach to education extends beyond the fundamentals of Literacy and Maths, ensuring that our pupils receive a holistic and enriching learning experience. This includes engaging lessons in Science, History, Geography, Art and PSHE. Our pupils also benefit from specialist teaching in Spanish, Music, Dance, and Drama. We understand the importance of physical activity for our children’s physical and mental health and wellbeing. Therefore, a significant part of our curriculum is devoted to PE, including swimming, games, and tennis sessions. pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Excellence - Private School In Charterhouse Square
pageCache.text:
Academic Excellence
Prepared for what's next.
It is not down to chance that our pupils enjoy success in the classroom and later exams. It is built on superb teaching and high expectations. Parents send their children to Charterhouse Square School because we offer superb preparation for senior school within a friendly and supportive environment. Year after year, our girls and boys leave the school with much-coveted places at some of London’s finest schools. They also leave with the personal skills necessary to make the most of the opportunities they have earned.
Our success is not down to chance – or a selective entry policy.
Our bespoke and evolving curriculum is carefully designed to keep our pupils a year ahead of what is expected for their age group. Reviewed annually, it combines academic rigour with creativity, self-expression, and holistic development. From Nursery to Year 6, highly qualified and specialist teachers enrich the curriculum, tailoring lessons to meet the ever-changing needs of each individual child. This dynamic approach ensures a Charterhouse Square education remains both progressive and purposeful.
We prioritise building strong connections between teachers and pupils. With our no-uniform policy, pupils feel seen, understood, and supported by teachers who can adapt lessons to their unique learning journeys. Our classrooms foster a sense of mutual respect and trust, allowing children to thrive academically and personally.
Every child is different, and we celebrate that. Through ongoing progress reviews, our teachers identify areas where pupils need greater challenge or additional support. For example, able mathematicians in Years 5 and 6 are invited to join our Maths XL Club, where they are stretched and inspired to tackle more advanced concepts. Using mixed-ability groupings, children choose their level of challenge, guiding their own learning while reflecting on their progress. Teachers act as facilitators, scaffolding and extending pupils as needed. For those who need additional support, our Learning Support Team works closely with children to put tailored strategies in place.
From an early age, we empower pupils to take ownership of their learning. They manage their homework, organise their belongings, and develop self-discipline. By fostering independence, resilience, and a growth mindset, we prepare children to confidently navigate new challenges and embrace opportunities.

The Early Year Foundation Stage
Throughout the Early Years, we continuously assess your child's progress. In the final term of Reception, we complete the official Early Years Foundation Stage Profile, measuring attainment in key learning areas aligned with the Early Learning Goals (ELGs). To achieve a Good Level of Development (GLD), children must meet the ELGs in personal, social, and emotional development, language and communication, physical development, literacy, and mathematics.
Progress Test in Maths and English
Our pupils’ academic progress is carefully monitored through annual National Standardised tests in English and Mathematics. The Progress Test in English (PTE) assesses pupils' technical English skills, including spelling, grammar, punctuation, and reading comprehension. The Progress Test in Maths (PTM) monitors their mathematical skills and knowledge in areas such as number, shape, data handling, and algebra, as well as their mathematical reasoning and problem-solving abilities. The results presented below show age-standardised scores, with the red dashed line indicating the national average of 100. Notably, our pupils have consistently achieved scores significantly above the national average.

pageCache.text:
Wellbeing & Pastoral Care
Supported to thrive
At Charterhouse Square School, we are determined to help every child develop courage, honesty, kindness, and confidence. We believe these are the core values to help children succeed in a competitive world. As such, we pride ourselves on providing an exceptional pastoral care offering.
Our commitment to comprehensive emotional support.
A fundamental element of our wellbeing offering involves maintaining a strong sense of community among our staff and pupils, fostering a true sense of family. Our school community is closely knit, where everyone, including parents, pupils, and staff form meaningful connections that create a supportive and inclusive environment. As part of our commitment to well-being, we integrate mental health into our daily routines and overall school ethos. This includes daily emotional check-ins, where pupils can share how they are feeling upon entering the classroom, ensuring immediate support if needed. Throughout the school, worry boxes are placed in key locations, allowing pupils to confidentially express their concerns. These are checked daily by staff to ensure no issue goes unnoticed. We also follow the Jigsaw PSHE (Personal, Social, Health, and Economic) programme, which includes weekly lessons that focus on emotions, behaviours, and health. These lessons equip pupils with the tools to understand and manage their mental well-being.
One of our dedicated staff members is a trained counsellor who provides support for pupils dealing with friendship troubles, nerves around starting senior school, and general anxieties.
Throughout the school, we have worry boxes situated in key locations. These boxes are checked daily, allowing pupils to express their concerns and anxieties in a safe and confidential manner.
We actively involve our pupils in shaping our well-being initiatives. This includes conducting pupil surveys and holding school council meetings to gather their insights and feedback, ensuring that their voices are heard and valued.
To support the physical and mental wellbeing of our pupils, we provide freshly cooked, nutritious meals on-site to ensure our pupils are energised for success.
We have two staff members trained in the Drawing and Talking programme, enabling them to provide support to pupils with clear social or emotional needs.
Staff are passionate about developing pupils' academic progress and emotional wellbeing and are committed to carefully monitoring every child's journey as they progress through the school. We have four trained Mental Health First Aiders who can identify and address concerns early, ensuring a proactive approach to well-being. Our SENCOs work closely with pupils facing challenges such as friendship issues or communication difficulties, providing targeted interventions to support their emotional and social development.
The dedicated teacher is the first person your child sees every day, this creates familiarity and trust between pupil and teacher. Through daily check-ins, teachers promote emotional awareness and act swiftly to address any concerns. Our teachers are deeply committed to understanding each child's personal and academic journey. This insight enables them to provide encouragement and challenges that help pupils make the most of the many opportunities at Charterhouse Square School, from extracurricular activities and sports to creative pursuits. In doing so, they play a pivotal role in shaping confident, well-rounded individuals.
When a child joins Charterhouse Square School, the parents become part of the community. We develop a relationship based on honesty and trust, with the child at the heart of our conversations. Parents are warmly welcomed to attend sports fixtures, music recitals, drama productions, and social events, reinforcing the sense of family that defines our school. Our strong parent-school relationship ensures a collaborative effort in supporting every child’s well-being and success.
We deliver a well-rounded PSHE programme that prepares pupils for the pressures and challenges of the outside world. Our Jigsaw PSHE curriculum addresses critical areas of development, including emotions, behaviours, and health. These lessons are complemented by initiatives like mindfulness and yoga sessions, teaching pupils relaxation and stress management techniques.

Admissions Process for All Other Year Groups
Joining us is straightforward.
Charterhouse Square prides itself on ensuring a smooth, open and professional admissions process. While most children join us in Nursery, occasional places do become available in other year groups. We warmly encourage families to get in touch at any stage to discuss availability. Our Admissions Team work all year round to ensure enquiries are dealt with quickly and efficiently. Our steps to enrolment are outlined here and aim to give you a sense of the steps we go through at Charterhouse Square to ensure that we are the right school for your child.
If you have any questions about joining us at Charterhouse Square School, please click the link below to get in touch.
Experience the welcoming atmosphere of Charterhouse Square first-hand by joining us for a Personal Tour or an Open Event. These events offer an excellent opportunity to meet our Headteacher, interact with classroom teachers and pupils, and provide you with the chance to ask any questions that will help you feel confident about your child fulfilling their potential with us.
When you are ready to take the next step, simply complete the online application form and pay a registration fee of £180 (non-refundable). This will enable us to start our admissions process to ensure that we can meet your child's needs.

Cognita schools provide a uniquely global education.

Continuous improvement is at the heart of the Cognita Way.
Our Global Education Team is comprised of leaders based in each of Cognita’s four global regions and together they utilise evidence – from within our group as well as external sources – to drive outstanding educational practice across all our schools. pageCache.pageTitle: Creative and Self-Expression - Charterhouse Square School
pageCache.text:
Creative and Self-Expression
Inspiring individuality and growth.
We believe that creativity is at the core of individuality and self-discovery. That’s why self-expression through art, music, drama, sports, and other creative pursuits is a vital part of our curriculum. By encouraging pupils to explore a range of expressive activities, both in the classroom and beyond, we nurture their confidence, creativity, and personal growth. Throughout the school day, pupils actively participate in various creative and physical activities - from art, drama, and dance to sports and music groups. They have the chance to think creatively, build teamwork skills, and express themselves through a wide range of channels, including peripatetic music lessons, school clubs, and co-curricular activities. Each experience is designed to empower our pupils to embrace who they are and discover new ways to connect with the world around them.
Music & Drama
Visual Arts
Sport & Physical Activity
Music & Drama
Our pupils benefit from weekly music and drama lessons taught by specialist staff. These dedicated sessions allow pupils to explore their artistic abilities and develop their creative skills. Each year, all classes participate in a school production, providing pupils with opportunities to boost their confidence while engaging in theatrical experiences. In Early Years, our pupils have the wonderful opportunity to attend London Symphony Orchestra (LSO) concerts, which allows them to explore the world of music and performance. Throughout the year, we also host various external companies at our school to enhance our pupils' theatrical experiences and ignite their imaginations. These include the Little Angel Puppet Theatre and OperaEd, who provide them with an immersive experience in the world of opera. Our Upper House host the prestigious Premier Performance in the stunning St Giles’ Church, Cripplegate. This event allows our pupils to showcase their talents, including singing, recitation, or playing musical instruments of their choice.
We offer private music lessons in a variety of instruments, including:
Our commitment to artistic expression extends to the visual arts.
All our pupils benefit from weekly art lessons, which are taught by either specialist staff or their class teachers. Our Creative Studio opens up a world of possibilities for pupils to explore various artistic mediums, including clay, papier mâché, pastels, charcoal, glass/silk painting. These art lessons are often linked to topic work, like creating letter illuminations when studying the Medieval period or crafting 3D robot creations while reading 'The Iron Man.' We also embrace the exciting world of Digital Art, where pupils experiment with innovative techniques like Pixel Pointillism, using programmes such as PaintZ on iPads. Our Art Club is highly popular among our pupils, offering them the chance to develop skills like sewing or observational drawing. We believe in providing our pupils with exposure to the rich world of art beyond the classroom. They have the opportunity to visit local galleries such as The National Gallery and The Tate, where they can appreciate and draw inspiration from some of the world's most remarkable collections of paintings.
Sport & Physical Activity
The importance of activity.
We understand that being active is essential for personal growth and self-expression. At Charterhouse Square School, sports and physical activities are about more than fitness; they’re opportunities for children to discover their strengths, build resilience, and learn the value of teamwork. With a commitment to active learning, our children participate in significantly more physical activities than most other prep schools. We play around three times as much as state school primaries. Our children enjoy up to four hours of PE and sport each week – and that’s on top of the 40 minutes of exercise they get at lunchtime when we are permitted to use the garden in Charterhouse Square. From Year 2 onwards, all of our children enjoy a weekly swimming session at Ironmonger Row Baths, a short walk away from the school. They will also take a short coach trip to enjoy the fantastic astroturf facilities at Coram’s Fields.
Specialist facilities and teachers.
Our pupils receive training from experienced and qualified coaches across a wide variety of sports, including football, hockey, netball, tag rugby, athletics, cricket, rounders, swimming, and tennis. By participating in these activities, they learn to set personal goals, support their peers, and appreciate the value of teamwork. Each session, whether in PE, aerobics, or team practice, is a chance for them to develop self-confidence and explore their individual interests. Sports events are a cherished part of our school’s calendar, with our annual swimming gala in the autumn and whole-school sports day in July, offering our pupils the opportunity to showcase their growth and celebrate their achievements with family and friends. We also compete in inter-school athletics, football, netball, and swimming tournaments and host fixtures with local schools, creating memorable experiences for our pupils and their supporters.
Sport in action
Building confidence through communication.
We believe that strong communication skills are essential for self-expression, personal growth, and future success. Oracy is a key part of our curriculum, empowering pupils to articulate their thoughts clearly, listen actively, and engage meaningfully with others. Through structured activities like debating, philosophy for children, and discussions on current affairs, our pupils explore complex topics, learning to think critically and present their ideas confidently. Our pupils also participate in presentations on chosen subjects, giving them valuable experience in expressing their interests and perspectives. These activities build a strong foundation in public speaking, collaboration, and critical thinking - skills they draw upon in all areas of school life. In addition, pupils have the opportunity to serve as tour guides on Viewing Days, gaining practical experience in speaking confidently with unfamiliar adults and sharing their pride in our school. To further prepare pupils for interviews and beyond, we emphasise oracy skills as essential tools for effective communication. We are immensely proud of the poise and confidence with which our pupils engage with both their peers and adults. Through oracy, our pupils develop the ability to communicate thoughtfully and authentically, enriching their self-expression and preparing them for success in all their future endeavours.

pageCache.pageTitle: Design & Architecture Project - Charterhouse Square School
pageCache.text:
Designing beyond the classroom
At Charterhouse Square School, learning extends beyond the classroom and into the city around us. As part of Clerkenwell Design Week, our pupils became designers of their own environment – exploring how architecture shapes the way we live, move and connect.
Set in one of London’s most design-rich neighbourhoods, this project invited pupils to engage directly with the world around them. Inspired by the Barbican and its surrounding streets, they reimagined spaces through creativity, purpose and a thoughtful approach to the future.
The Process
This was a hands-on, multi-layered design journey. Pupils began by observing the spaces around them – how people use them, how they feel, and how they could be improved. From there, they translated their thinking into sketches, developed concepts using digital tools, and brought their ideas to life through sculptural model-making. Each stage encouraged experimentation, problem-solving and independent thinking, mirroring the process of real-world design.
Hear the thinking behind the designs
Every model and concept tells a story.
Through the videos below, our pupils share their ideas, explain their design choices, and reflect on what they discovered along the way – from sustainability and community to the small details that shape how a space is experienced.
Connecting learning to the real world
Projects like this reflect our belief that education should feel relevant, purposeful and connected.
By engaging with the built environment around them, pupils begin to understand their role within it – not just as learners, but as thinkers, creators and future contributors to the world beyond school.
Through this experience, they develop the skills that sit at the heart of a Charterhouse Square education:
Creative thinking
Collaboration
Communication
Environmental awareness
Confidence
